title: A convoy north-west of Amami-Ōshima, 2 December 1944
eyebrow: The East China Sea · SEA DEVIL's second war patrol

participants.name: Convoy
participants.note: as SEA DEVIL saw it, at least seven ships with four or more escorts, course 230 at 8 knots; the Imperial Navy's summary names one ship of it, Hawaii Maru, bound from Moji for Takao, and CD-66 as an escort. Secondary sources call it MI-29, which no record read here names

paras.text: SEA DEVIL's three attacks on a southbound convoy in the early hours of 2 December 1944, as typed on her attack sheets, beside the Imperial Navy's summary of the night: the army transport Hawaii Maru, with 3,648 troops aboard, torpedoed and sunk at 0430.

SEA DEVIL fired four bow torpedoes at 0414 I (all missed), two more at 0424 I, which she saw hit a large ship that listed and sank rapidly (she took it for a tanker of 10,000 tons), and four stern torpedoes at 0429 I, one of which hit a large freighter she claimed probably sunk. The Navy's summary for the day has one ship lost: Hawaii Maru, an army-requisitioned transport of 9,500 tons carrying 3,648 troops, 50 vehicles and 60 landing craft from Moji for Takao, torpedoed at 0430 I about 120 miles north-west of Amami-Ōshima, sunk; and at 0945 the escort CD-66 depth-charged a submarine it had closed to 100 m (p. 2) [[cite:jacar:C16120660300]]. Six minutes after the Attack 2 hits, Hawaii Maru is paired with that attack as probable. The summary's place is a round bearing and distance some 70 nm from SEA DEVIL's; it names no second ship, so Attack 3's hit is unaccounted for. Secondary sources give the convoy a second loss, Akigawa Maru; the requisitioned-ship tables' ship of that name is another, sunk in April 1944.

Positions are SEA DEVIL's own; her attack sheets give the same position for all three attacks (30-51N 128-45E), and the convoy contact at 2351 I on the 1st is typed at it too. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position.
SEA DEVIL kept zone I (−9) in the East China Sea, the Japanese records' zone, so the two sides' times compare as typed.

The convoy's own record: the 1st Surface Escort Division's diary has no December 1944 part on JACAR, and no CD-66 record of December was found. Hawaii Maru was army-requisitioned, so she is not in the Imperial Navy's ship tables.

SEA DEVIL's second war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74843922). The Navy's day-by-day summary of escort and anti-submarine events, December 1944, via JACAR (C16120660300, National Institute for Defense Studies). Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.title: Hawaii Maru
events.words: 0430: Hawaii Maru (army-requisitioned passenger ship, type A, 9,500 tons, carrying 3,648 troops, 50 vehicles and 60 landing craft), southbound from Moji for Takao, torpedoed by an enemy submarine 120 miles north-west of Amami-Ōshima | (Result) sunk

events.note: The summary's narrative for the 2nd (read at 350 dpi). Six minutes after SEA DEVIL's Attack 2 (0424 I, two timed hits on what she took for a large tanker, seen listing and sinking rapidly) and one minute after Attack 3 (0429 I). No position in figures: 120 miles north-west of Amami-Ōshima (about 28-20N 129-30E) puts it near 29-45N 128-00E, some 70 nm west-south-west of SEA DEVIL's sheets (30-51N 128-45E); the bearing and distance are round figures. The summary names no convoy and no second ship sunk that night

words.type_attack: Contacted first by SJ radar. Tracked and dived ahead of convoy for normal night periscope submerged approach. Used T.D.C. and spread by "continuous bearing method" with periscope.
words.description: At least a seven ship convoy with four or more unknown-type escorts. Contact made by SJ radar at range of 39,500 yards. Visibility from poor to very good (dependent on obscurity of moon).

words.determined_by: One timed hit which was very loud. Heard through the hull what sounded like debris falling overhead and on deck. Sound heard breaking up noises on target bearing.
words.target_line: Target Draft: Unknown Course: 230°T Speed: 8 knots Range: 1350 yds.
words.own_ship: Speed: 5 knots Course: 053°T Depth: 60 feet Angle: 2° down
words.note: Stern tubes 7-10, Mk 23s. The typed tracks (97P-104P) are about 50° from what own course 053 and the typed gyros (202-210) give against target course 230 (check_attacks.py: 147-155P); own course is typed clearly as 053°T, five minutes after Attack 2's 328°T, so one of the three figures is not what was used. Kept as typed. The hit is tube 10's
